An earlier dark slate (#3D4A5C) was unreadable at that size because a dark fill merges with the island's own black coastline stroke. USE A HIGH-VALUE HIGH-CHROMA COLOR AND GIVE IT AN INSET; no hue alone can carry 47 pixels. DRAW ONLY ON MAPS SET AFTER THE COURT'S FOUNDING. Korea submitted Jeju-do as neutral ground to be legally shared among KOREA; JAPAN and THE SINIAN FEDERATION. Give it its own color - distinct from all three parents (Korea purple; Japan rose; Sinian cyan) - and its own legend entry naming the three. It is a first-order subdivision (Jeju Special Self-Governing Province) so drawing it out of Korea does NOT break the whole-subdivision rule. TIMING: the Court was an established institution at least one full generation before its April 27 2318 ruling; while Korea's reunification and the Federation's founding were at least three and possibly four generations before 2318 - so there is a window of roughly two generations in which the unified map is correct but Jeju is still ordinary Korean territory. The existing late-era nations map sits in that window.
